chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil

Similar to it, except that he said: I said to Jamil, 'And the woman?' He said: Our companions have narrated it, namely 'Umbasah ibn Mus'ab and Sawrah ibn Kulaib, from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them.

key_terms.أَحَدُهُمَا: One of the two (referring to one of the two Imams, likely al-Sadiq or al-Kazim)
key_terms.أَصْحَابُنَا: Our companions (referring to the prominent Shia narrators of this era)
key_terms.فَالْمَرْأَةُ: And the woman (specific inquiry about the female subject)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman regarding the preceding legal matter according to the narrations of 'Umbah and Sawrah?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the rigorous chain of transmission (*isnad*) characteristic of Shia jurisprudence, linking the companion Jamil to prominent narrators like 'Umbasah and Sawrah. It underscores the reliability of these specific authorities in establishing legal precedents, likely concerning the *iddah* (waiting period) or divorce, by affirming that the ruling is firmly rooted in the teachings of the Imams.
